subject: Compute tiering vs. contract duration for private offer - NimbleStats
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura@nimblestats.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimblestats.com
Date: 2027-03-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring private offer options for NimbleStats

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the latency numbers look promising for our inference-heavy workloads. Procurement asked me to follow up with concrete options for an AWS Marketplace private offer.

Quick background: our CFO prefers annual commitments for budgeting, but our engineering team wants flexibility: 6–9 month pilots with the option to scale bursts. Two asks from procurement:
- Can Redwood split the commitment into a firm annual baseline + burst/overage usage pricing?
- What buyer-level approvals on AWS Marketplace are required for us to accept a private offer (we have multiple BU CFOs)?

If you can send a sample structure (pricing table + who signs on the buyer side), that would help us move to our legal/procurement review.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
NimbleStats

--
Attachment: initial_requirements.docx (docx stub)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@nimblestats.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring private offer options for NimbleStats

Laura — appreciate the clear asks.

Short answers up front:
1) Yes — we can structure a private offer with a firm annual baseline (committed vCPU-hours / token budget) plus an overage tier billed at a higher per-unit rate. This preserves a predictable baseline while letting you burst.
2) Buyer approvals: typically CFO signoff + procurement approval in the buyer account are needed to accept an AWS Marketplace private offer. If multiple BU CFOs will sign, we can set the offer to require a single canonical buyer account to accept and then coordinate internal chargebacks off-platform; alternately, we can create separate private offers per BU.

Attached is a quick pricing sketch and a sample private_offer_draft_NS-7832.pdf. Highlights:
- Baseline: 100k instance-hours/year at $X/hour (1 year term)
- Flexible burst: pay-as-you-go at $Y/hour above baseline
- Co-sell credit split: propose 30% credit to AWS / 70% to Redwood (draft — negotiable)

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa / Dev and I will prepare two concrete templates: (A) single-offer canonical buyer with internal billing, (B) multi-offer per BU. We'll include the DocuSign workflow and an estimated timeline for AWS private offer activation (~5–10 business days after buyer acceptance and verification).

I'll attach pricing_model_v2.xlsx with worked examples. Can you confirm whether the CFO wants a single canonical buyer or separate BU offers?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet); private_offer_draft_NS-7832.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura@nimblestats.com>
Date: 2027-03-17T09:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring private offer options for NimbleStats

Looping in procurement playbook items and activation cadence.

Aditya — small notes from an ops/finance standpoint:
- If we go single canonical buyer, we should include a clear purchase order (PO) mapping and a billing reconciliation appendix so NimbleStats' internal chargeback doesn't create disputes. I'll draft a PO appendix with seat/instance mapping.
- On approvals: buyer acceptance on AWS typically needs an admin in the buyer account + procurement/CFO approval for large commits. If the CFOs are separate by BU, recommend separate private offers to avoid delays — acceptance per BU is faster than internal signoffs across multiple stakeholders.
- Co-sell credits: we can be flexible. For larger baseline commitments (> $200k ARR), propose 35/65 to make AWS co-sell motion cleaner.

Action items I can take: draft PO appendix + sample DocuSign flow. Dev — can you confirm SLO language for burst capacity and whether we can cap burst latency guarantees (i.e., best-effort above baseline)?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: po_appendix_template.docx (docx stub)

From: Procurement Team <procurement@nimblestats.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-18T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring private offer options for NimbleStats

Aditya / Marissa — thanks for the examples.

Two quick clarifications from our side:
1) We prefer separate offers per BU to keep budget accountability clean. Please produce separate PDFs for each BU with the same baseline/burst terms but separate acceptance windows.
2) Who will be the signing authority for AWS acceptance? Our legal wants to know the AWS Marketplace user role (admin or purchaser) that needs to click accept, and whether DocuSign will also be required after acceptance for on-paper signatures.

If you can send the BU-specific PDFs and the DocuSign flow, procurement will route for CFO signoff. We're targeting decision by 2027-03-25.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
NimbleStats

--
